subject: DPA kickoff: EscrowAnalytics integration + subprocessor whitelist
messages:
From: Paul Turner <paul.turner@escrowanalytics.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Integration: DPA + subprocessors for EscrowAnalytics data flow

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As mentioned, EscrowAnalytics will be integrating Redwood's inference API to power redaction and classification for documents held in our escrow service. Before we can run a short pilot we need a couple of things from Redwood: your current DPA (template is fine), a list of subprocessors you expect to engage for this integration (including cloud infra / logging / analytics vendors), and a simple dataflow map showing where personal data lands and how long it's retained.

Our legal counsel (cc'd) prefers AdobeSign for execution but we can do DocuSign if that's your standard. Target timeline: pilot contract in two weeks, execution by mid-December. Can you confirm the below and share the files?

- Redwood DPA template
- Subprocessor list + intended roles
- Dataflow mapping (CSV ok)
- SOC2 or similar attestation (if available)

Happy to jump on a quick follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Paul Turner
Head of Product
EscrowAnalytics

Attachments referenced: none in this message

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Paul Turner <paul.turner@escrowanalytics.com>
Cc: Kelsea Moore <kelsea@trlaw.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration: DPA + subprocessors for EscrowAnalytics data flow

Paul — thanks for the summary and the timeline. Attaching our standard DPA template and a starter dataflow CSV (see attachments). A few quick notes:

- We will provide a subprocessor list; currently planned subprocessors are cloud compute (RedCloud Inc.), telemetry/logging (BeamMetrics), and hosted metrics (Metricly). Ill confirm versions and regions for each.
- Redwood supports SCCs for EU transfers; we'll include language for that.
- SOC2 Type II is attached (2025 report).
- We can execute via AdobeSign; our legal ops team can generate an Adobe flow if you prefer that over DocuSign.

Im looping in Mina from Legal and Laura from Contract Ops to review for any client-specific redlines. Mina/Laura — could you review the attached template and propose any required edits for EscrowAnalytics's use case?

Next steps: I will confirm subprocessors and provide the subprocessor whitelist by EOD tomorrow. If we need a mutual action plan for the pilot, I can draft one.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.docx; escrow-dataflow-mapping.csv; SOC2_cert_2025.pdf

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Integration: DPA + subprocessors for EscrowAnalytics data flow

Mina/Laura — forwarding initial request from EscrowAnalytics. Key asks: DPA template review, subprocessor whitelist, and support for AdobeSign execution. Client hopes to sign mid-December.

Quick context: the integration touches PII in documents well process for redaction/classification. Theyre a US-headquartered escrow provider with EU customers, so SCCs + clear retention windows are required.

Requested from Legal:
- Review Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.docx and flag any clauses that need strengthening for an escrow/third-party data holder use case (particularly restricted use, audit rights, and breach timelines).
- Confirm whether we can provide the subprocessor list as a whitelist (they prefer a pre-approved list) or must stick to our standard notice-and-approve workflow.
- Suggest any short-term concessions to keep pilot timeline (e.g., limited audit rights during pilot, pre-approved subprocessors for pilot only).

Thanks — can you reply with redline comments inline or a short summary by EOD tomorrow?

-Neha

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Integration: DPA + subprocessors for EscrowAnalytics data flow

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed the attached DPA and sketched the following recommended approach for the EscrowAnalytics pilot:

1) Data transfer: include SCCs + a short clause permitting transfer under our Binding Corporate Rules (if/when available) as fallback. For pilot, SCCs are fine.

2) Subprocessors: for pilots we can offer a "pilot whitelist" for the list youve provided (RedCloud Inc., BeamMetrics, Metricly) on the condition were notified before any changes and that any additional subprocessors need prior written consent. For production well revert to our standard published subprocessor list with notice window.

3) Audit and access: propose a limited audit right during pilot (desktop review + SOC2 copy) rather than full on-site audits. We will provide the SOC2 attestation (attached) and agree to a documented checkpoint for audit requests.

4) Retention and deletion: recommend explicit retention buckets in the DPA (pilot = 30 days; production configurable up to 365 days) with an option to shorten for EscrowAnalytics.

5) Breach notification: keep our 72-hour notification obligation but add a pilot-specific SLA to acknowledge receipt and an initial triage call within 24 hours.

6) Execution: we support both AdobeSign and DocuSign. If EscrowAnalytics prefers AdobeSign, well generate the agreement from our contract ops tenant and send the AdobeSign link.

Ive attached an annotated copy of the template with inline comments (see SharePoint link above). Laura, can you prepare an AdobeSign agreement flow and target a signing request for Dec 10? Neha, I suggest we confirm subprocessor regions (us/eu) before sending the flow.

-Mina
General Counsel (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: annotated DPA (stored on internal SharePoint link)

From: Paul Turner <paul.turner@escrowanalytics.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Kelsea Moore <kelsea@trlaw.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration: DPA + subprocessors for EscrowAnalytics data flow

Neha / Mina — thanks, this is helpful and actionable. We accept the pilot whitelist approach for the three subprocessors listed. Two quick follow-ups before you generate the AdobeSign request:

- Can you confirm the RedCloud compute region will be us-west-2 for the pilot? We need that for our internal data residency controls.
- We'll proceed with the limited audit approach; Kelsea will sign off on the SOC2 review.

If RedCloud is us-west-2, were happy for you to generate the AdobeSign flow and well aim to have internal approvals completed by Dec 8 so signing on Dec 10 is fine. Please include the escrow-dataflow-mapping.csv as an exhibit in the Adobe package.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Paul Turner
Head of Product, EscrowAnalytics

Attachments: none
